title: Prime cyclic coefficient is a retract of a nonzero ring quotient
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $h:Y\to X$ a morphism of schemes, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $r$ a prime natural number which is not a unit in $\Lambda$ [def-pc-scheme]. Write $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$ and use the constant module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $R^qh_*\underline{\Lambda/(r)}=0$, then $R^qh_*\underline{P_r/(r)}=0$, with higher direct images computed in the corresponding module-sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Tag 0F08 (proof, cyclic-coefficient reduction); Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree); Tag 0739 (lemma-colimit), with the arbitrary-ring coefficient argument explicitly supplied here

proof.text: Set V=Lambda/(r). Ideal.span_singleton_ne_top and Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff make V nontrivial. The image of r is zero, so CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero makes it a ZMod r algebra using ZMod.castHom. Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one gives phi with phi(1)=1. Since phi(a*1)=a, this splits the additive inclusion of ZMod r into V. In P=ULift(ZMod r), r=0, so Ideal.quotEquivOfEq, RingEquiv.quotientBot and ULift.ringEquiv identify P/(r) with ZMod r. Compose these maps to obtain the additive Retract of P/(r) from V (private quotient_retract).

Forgetting ModuleCat coefficients is left adjoint: express it as restriction along integers to Lambda, followed by the equivalence from integer modules to abelian groups. ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj and Functor.isLeftAdjoint_of_iso establish this explicitly, so the functor preserves sheafification. Apply Mathlib constantCommuteCompose to identify the underlying constant module sheaves with the constant abelian sheaves (private preservesSheafification_forget_modules).

The unit-route injective acyclicity lemma remains imported. The needed derived comparison is now stated as the general forgetful higher-direct-image isomorphism, which is a distinct part of the argument. Apply it to the two coefficient rings and compose with the constant-sheaf isomorphisms. Transfer the assumed module-valued zero object to the abelian derived image of the constant V sheaf.

Map the additive retract through the constant abelian sheaf functor and then the composite single-in-degree-zero, derived abelian direct image, and degree-q homology functor. The identity of the retract factors through the zero target, hence equals zero. Transfer this zero object back by the prime-coefficient comparison isomorphism. The faithful coefficient forgetful functor preserves zero morphisms objectwise, and reflects a zero identity by map_injective. This proves the original conclusion, in all integer degrees.
